properties.name: Arkau Municipal Outdoor Pool
properties.description:
The 50 x 15 m pool is divided into a swimming pool and a fun pool (non-swimmers). The fun pool has a wide slide, a water spout, as well as floor bubbles and massage jets.

There is also a 120 m² paddling pool for children.  In addition, there is a mud pit, a climbing frame, and a nest swing for the little ones. The large sunbathing lawn, which is equipped with child-friendly play equipment, offers plenty of opportunities for fun and relaxation with table tennis tables, a beach volleyball court, and a kiosk.

properties.name: Baroque church of St. Maria
properties.description:
The 51 m high onion dome is the landmark of the baroque church of St. Maria, visible from afar.

A church had already been built on this site in the 13th century, which was demolished in 1763 and replaced by the current church in 1764 - 1768. The rococo building is one of the most important buildings of this era in Baden. Not far from the church is a lime tree planted in 1737. Together with the former rectory from 1758 and the Nepomuk Chapel to the south of the parish church, a former mortuary chapel built in 1503 and rebuilt in 1745/46, the center of Kappelwindeck boasts a remarkable ensemble of buildings.

properties.name: Carl Netter Observation Tower
properties.description:
Zwischen Bühl-Altschweier und Bühl-Eisental liegt der 10 m hohe Aussichtsturm, von dem sich eine herrliche Aussicht über Rheinebene, Reben und zu den Schwarzwaldbergen bietet.

Der Turm aus Metall wurde 1902 zu Ehren von Großherzog Friedrich errichtet. Stifter des Turmes waren die Brüder Adolph und Carl Leopold Netter, die um die Jahrhundertwende mit ihrem Stahlunternehmen die Weltmärkte erobert hatten und die Stadt Bühl mit Stiftungen und Schenkungen unterstützten. Der Turm ist jederzeit zugänglich.

properties.name: Black Forest pool
properties.description:
The Schwarzwaldbad Bühl is a combined indoor and outdoor pool with 3 indoor and 6 outdoor pools with a water surface area of over 2000 square meters.

The indoor pool includes a swimmers' pool, a non-swimmers' pool and a toddlers' pool. A service station with hot and cold drinks and various snacks is available in the warming hall with a separate relaxation room.  
In addition to the swimmers' and non-swimmers' pool, the outdoor pool offers a children's pool with two water slides and a diving facility. The spacious outdoor area offers a wonderful view of the Black Forest. The outdoor pool also has a playground with two large wooden boats, a beach volleyball court and a children's paddling pool with a sun awning for the little ones.

properties.name: City Museum
properties.description:
The town museum has been housed in a former bakery since 2010. The 17th century building is one of the oldest residential buildings to have survived in Bühl.  

The collection guides visitors through the eventful history of the town from the first traces of settlement to the 20th century. The first floor is dedicated to economic history: market and trade, guilds, crafts and manufactories, industry and companies. The exhibition on the top floor provides an insight into the lithographic workshop of Johannes Lohmüller (1830-1918), the last portrait lithographer in Baden. Here you can see the Lohmüller family's original photo studio, where visitors can have their picture taken in the style of the Wilhelminian era. The basement is dedicated to religious history: Catholic, Protestant and Jewish religion as well as the history of Jewish citizens from the 16th century to the deportation in 1940.  
Guided tours and educational museum activities are offered by the City History Institute.

properties.name: Parish church of St. Peter & Paul
properties.description:
The Catholic parish church of St. Peter and Paul, built in 1872-1877 by architect Karl Dernfeld, offers space for around 650 worshippers.

The church is 60 m long, 24 m wide and has a 63 m high openwork tower. The parishioners donated altars in the neo-Gothic style, of which only the sculptures remain today. In addition to the building deed and Baden coins, a bottle of Affentaler red wine 1870 and a bottle of white wine 1865 were placed in the foundation stone.

properties.name: Imperial City Museum in the Old Hospital
properties.description:
The Imperial City Museum in Bad Wimpfen brings the city's development after the fall of the Staufer dynasty to life on three floors. The Old Hospital in Bad Wimpfen The Old Hospital was founded before 1230 by the Knights Hospitaller and later taken over by the Order of the Holy Spirit. It developed into one of the largest hospitals in southern Germany. In the 15th century, it was divided into a spiritual and a civil hospital. The convent house, built in 1775, served as the monastery and hospital wing of the Order of the Holy Spirit. This classicist building impresses with its decorative order coat of arms in the Langgasse.

Today's hospital complex comprises the medieval stone building, the attached north and east wings, and an extension on Hauptstraße. Particularly noteworthy is the Alemannic half-timbered structure, which is one of the oldest in the city. Imperial City Museum Today, the Old Hospital houses the Imperial City Museum with an exhibition on the imperial history of Bad Wimpfen.  

The exhibition focuses on: - The territory of the imperial city with a large model of the city - The city's relationship with the emperor and the empire - City law - Defense - Jurisdiction - Crafts and trade - Life in the imperial city - The Jewish community in Wimpfen - The history of the salt works - The history of the hospital system - The history of the Battle of Wimpfen
- Technology and forms of half-timbered construction Another highlight awaits visitors on the top floor: the Helfrich Collection with **over 400 historical cameras** – from the first pinhole camera to modern digital cameras. In addition to the museum, the municipal gallery and the culture and tourist information office are also located in the Old Hospital. The museum is sponsored by the Alt Wimpfen e.V. association.

Visitor information Opening hours: Daily from 10:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. and 2:00 p.m. to 5:00 p.m. Guided tours: Individual guided tours can be booked during opening hours through the Culture and Tourist Information Office.

properties.name: Leyk's Lotus Garden
properties.description: **Asian Water Garden.** The 3,000 square meter water garden on the southern edge of Rothenburg enchants visitors with its lush variety of exotic plants. Secluded seating areas surrounded by greenery, in the tea house, or on the viewing terrace allow visitors to quickly forget the outside world. **Offers:** Guided tours of the ceramics factory and garden by appointment. Cafe and gift shop on site. **Seasonal admission:** Year-round season ticket €2. **Opening hours**: April to December, Monday to Sunday, 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. (from October until 5 p.m.).

properties.name: Taubertal on the Eich
properties.description:
**Landscape park.** With its double bridge, Kobolzeller church, and numerous mills along the Tauber River, the Tauber Valley at Eich is the epitome of an English garden and was also internationally recognized as such around 1900.

**Other attractions:** Guided tour "Romantic Rothenburg – In the footsteps of the artists" only available in German and as a group tour with prior registration. Bronnenmühle "Helmes" beer garden, "Rothenburger Eich" vineyard, Europe's highest concentration of mills.

properties.name: Bad Mergentheim Castle Park
properties.description:
**Pre-Romantic, sentimental landscape garden in the English style.** In the park of Mergentheim Residential Palace, a romantic lake, varied bridges, and two pleasure pavilions invite visitors to linger. Meadows and groups of trees create interesting lines of sight. The palace museum and church are open to visitors.

**Offers:** Guided tours, café in the castle garden.

properties.name: Burggarten Rothenburg o.d.T.
properties.description:
**Park on the site of a former castle complex.**

A Staufer castle built here in 1142 on an exposed mountain spur high above the Tauber River was destroyed in the mid-14th century. Today, it is a Baroque and English garden with the best view of the city and the Tauber Valley. When you reach the castle garden through the castle gate, you can enjoy beautiful views of the Tauber Valley from the viewing platforms on the left and right. To the north, visitors can see the district of Detwang, whose church houses a wooden altar by Tilman Riemenschneider. Rothenburg was first mentioned in a document here in 960. A short hiking trail leads from the castle garden to Detwang, which should take about 20 minutes – you will also pass the Unter den Linden beer garden, located directly on the Tauber. The Topplerschlösschen castle also peeks out from behind the trees in the north. To the south, the castle garden offers views across the An der Eich vineyard to the Tauber Valley with the Kobolzeller church and the double bridge, as well as the hospital district on the opposite side with the striking dormers of the youth hostel (formerly a horse mill).

**Other offers**: Night watchman tour open to the public every evening during the high season at 8:00 p.m. (English) and 9:30 p.m. (German) €8 or €9 per person, Staufer stele and information board Stauferburg, Rothenburg Tower Trail.

**Offers:** Guided tours of the garden and sandstone quarry (from 7 people €6 / from 15 people €5), duration approx. 1 - 1.5 hours. **Admission:** Adults: €3,  
children and young people aged 5-15: €1.50, children under 5 free. **Opening hours:** Without prior registration, the garden is open without a guided tour from April to October on every second Sunday of the month between 2:00 p.m. and 6:00 p.m.

properties.name: Teutonic Order Castle Museum
properties.description:
From 1527 to 1809, Mergentheim Castle was the residence of the Grand Masters and German Masters of the Teutonic Order. In 1996, the Teutonic Order Museum was reopened here, covering an area of around 3,000 square meters. Artworks, models, objects, and texts vividly illustrate the history of the Teutonic Order from its beginnings in 1190 to the present day, as well as its activities in the Holy Land, Prussia, and the Holy Roman Empire.

The princely rooms of the castle give an impression of the former glory of the Teutonic Order. The Berwart staircase and columned hall from the Renaissance, the Rococo Götterzimmer (Hall of the Gods) and Neue Fürstenwohnung (New Prince's Apartment), and the classicist Kapitelsaal (Chapter Hall) and main staircase bear witness to the castle's eventful architectural history. The jewel of the residence is the castle church, to whose construction important artists such as Balthasar Neumann and François de Cuvilliès contributed. The history of Bad Mergentheim is shown from its time as a Frankish settlement to its development as a spa town. In addition, there is an exhibition consisting of medieval sculpture and panel painting, exotica, faience, alabaster and marble reliefs from the Renaissance and Baroque periods, precious small pieces of furniture, handicrafts and curiosities from Baron Carl Joseph von Adelsheim, as well as a collection of 40 doll's kitchens, doll's rooms and doll's houses, and toy shops (19th/20th century) in the castle. The Mörike Cabinet is located in the city history section. Among other things, it is dedicated to the seven-year stay of the Swabian poet.

properties.name: Local history museum "Eicher-Wilhelme Hus"
properties.description:
The Eicher-Wilhelme Hus is one of the few houses in Ottersweier that survived the devastating fire during the Palatinate War of Succession in 1689 and has been given a new lease of life as a museum.

The Eicher-Wilhelme Hus is one of the few houses in Ottersweier that survived the devastating fire during the Palatinate War of Succession in 1689 and has been given a new lease of life as a museum.

properties.name: Municipal Museum

Es widmet sich nicht nur der Stadtgeschichte, dem Handwerk der Munderkinger Bürstenmachern, der Postgeschichte, Munderkinger Persönlichkeiten sondern auch den Römern und Alemannen.

Darüber hinaus beherbergt das Museum eine umfangreiche Sammlung von Puppen und Puppenstuben sowie historisches Blechspielzeug. Diese lassen so manches Herz höher schlagen und wecken Erinnerungen an die eigene Kindheit.

properties.name: Themenjahr Stadt.Landschaft.Natur
properties.description:
Rothenburg ob der Tauber liegt eingebettet zwischen zwei charakteristischen Landschaften: der Frankenhöhe im Norden und dem Taubertal im Süden. Diese geologische und kulturelle Grenzlage prägt das Stadtbild bis heute. Rothenburg ob der Tauber markiert den Übergang zwischen der sanft gewellten Frankenhöhe und Hohenloher Ebene – hier entspringen zahlreiche Bäche, die sich tief in die Landschaft eingeschnitten haben.

Die Tauber hat über Jahrtausende ein eindrucksvolles Tal geformt, das heute zu den reizvollsten Flusslandschaften Süddeutschlands zählt.

Dieses Themenjahr öffnet Türen, die sonst verschlossen bleiben und führt dich an der Seite von Naturparkrangern, Winzern, Förstern, Märchenerzählern und Vereinen hinaus in die Natur, hinein in die Geschichte und mitten hinein in das Rothenburg-Gefühl.

Rothenburg ob der Tauber ist weit mehr als eine mittelalterliche Stadt mit weltberühmter Silhouette – sie ist eine Stadtlandschaft, ein gewachsenes Gesamtkunstwerk aus Kultur, Geschichte und Natur.  
Das komplette Programmheft gibt es hier zum Download.

properties.name: Johanniskirche
properties.description:
From 1600 to 1628, the interior of the church underwent a radical renovation; a west gallery was added, and the attic floors were converted into the city’s largest granary, for which a new flat ceiling was installed, resting on four massive columns.

During the Thirty Years’ War, the church served as a burial site for Catholic officers.

After the city was annexed by Bavaria, it was handed over to the newly formed small Catholic parish in 1803. The pastoral station was elevated to a curacy in 1827 and to a parish in 1893. After World War II, the church was restored to its current condition in two extensive renovation phases.

The Prehistoric Museum is the central museum for the UNESCO World Heritage Site "Caves and Ice Age Art of the Swabian Jura".

The urmu brings Ice Age life on the edge of the Swabian Jura to life. Visitors learn how skillful and inventive people were 40,000 years ago. In the treasure troves of Ice Age art, exciting originals open up a new approach to the culture of the Ice Age people.

The "Venus of Hohle Fels" - the oldest depiction of a human being in the world - can also be admired up close. The oldest musical instruments in the world can not only be viewed, but sound samples give an impression of the sonority of the flutes made from bird bones and mammoth ivory.

properties.description: In Rothenburg ob der Tauber, the craftswoman's widow Walburga is confronted with the challenges posed by the death of her last husband. She has to remarry quickly, otherwise she will have to leave her home. Who was she, how and where did she live, what did her everyday life look like and what customs, rules and punishments were there? All these questions are answered by "Walburga's Time Travel", which takes you back to around 1500 and takes you on an entertaining journey through the alleyways of Rothenburg to "her home", the "Old Rothenburg Craftsman's House" from 1270. Easter to October and December: Thursday, Friday, Saturday at 7 pm. Also as a group tour, meeting point: Town Hall entrance, duration: 60 minutes, languages: German and English. Information and contact: Christine Glindemann, Tel. 09861/938668

properties.name: St. Stephen's Monastery
properties.description:
Das ehemalige Stephanskloster ist eine Ruine auf dem Heiligenberg.

St. Stephan, neben St. Michael das zweite Kloster auf dem Heiligenberg, wurde um das Jahr 1090 von dem Benediktiner Arnold erbaut. Dieser war kurz zuvor in den Benediktiner-Orden eingetreten. Er errichtete sich eine Klause und eine Kapelle auf dem vorderen Gipfel des Aberinsberges.

Zundebold, Propst im nahe gelegenen Michaelskloster, fand Gefallen an der Zelle Arnolds und ließ vier Jahre später, mit Erlaubnis des Klosters Lorsch, an die Kirche Gebäude anfügen. Von hier aus konnte man jede Bewegung im Neckartal schon von weitem beobachten, denn die Kuppe war kahl. Durch Bau und Heizung war ein großer Teil des Waldes abgeholzt worden. Gleichzeitig wurde die alte Zisterne (das Heidenloch) wieder instand gesetzt. St. Stephan bekam einen eigenen Bezirk zugewiesen und war damit wirtschaftlich unabhängig.

properties.name: Philosopher's garden
properties.description:
A sun-drenched natural balcony with an abundance of exotic plants.

Here you can relax on one of the benches or on the beautiful lawns and get some fresh air while enjoying the view.

Due to the mild climate along the Philosophenweg, many plants from subtropical areas (e.g. almond trees, lemon trees and gingko trees) thrive here and have become native to this area.

properties.name: Carl Bosch Museum Heidelberg
properties.description: The Carl Bosch Museum in Heidelberg offers its visitors over 300m² of insights into the life and discoveries of Nobel Prize winner Carl Bosch.

properties.name: Philosopher's path
properties.description:
On the natural balcony of the Philosophenweg, every spectator sits in the front row and can take in nature and the view of the city at the same time.

Unprotected, the exotic plants thrive on this climatic island, which is one of the warmest places in Germany: Japanese woolly mistletoe and American cypress, Spanish broom and Portuguese cherry, lemon and pomegranate, bamboo, palm trees, pine trees. Everything blooms weeks earlier than in the valley. Scholars once walked here in stiff frock coats and relaxed their thoughts on a walk: the Heidelberg Philosophers' Path on the sunny slope of the Heiligenberg has led many to new insights, and in any case to unique views of Heidelberg. From this place in the sun, whose mild climate and vegetation are reminiscent of Tuscany, the "Heidelberg triad" of old town, river and mountains can be enjoyed at leisure.

properties.name: Heiliggeistkirche
properties.description:
At the beginning of the 13th century, a small Romanesque basilica Zum Heiligen Geist stood on the site of today's Heiliggeistkirche, which presumably fell victim to a fire at the beginning of the 14th century.

An early Gothic church was built in its place, in which the opening mass for the founding of Heidelberg University took place on October 18, 1386.

Under Ruprecht III, the choir of the church was demolished and replaced by a larger one.

The hall choir was completed in 1410, the nave with the substructure of the tower in 1441.

Louis III laid the foundations for the later famous Palatinate Library, the BIBLIOTECA PALATINA, by having the first books placed in the galleries of the Heiliggeistkirche.

During the reign of Louis V (1508-1544), the tower was further built and completed.

In the course of the Reformation, the church changed several times between Lutheran and Reformed-Calvinist denominations.

In 1563, the Heidelberg Catechism was created as a reformed confession.

With the Thirty Years' War and the conquest of Heidelberg by Catholic troops, the city and the church became Catholic for many years and Pope Gregory XV had the BIBLIOTECA PALATINA brought to Rome as spoils of war in 1623.

The church was severely damaged during the Palatinate-Orléans War of Succession in 1693.

Almost all of the tomb slabs of the Electors Palatine were destroyed; the one of Elector Ruprecht II has been preserved.

Of the once 5000 books and 3524 manuscripts, only 885 were returned to Heidelberg in 1816, all others remained in the Vatican.

In the following two centuries, both Catholics and Protestants laid claim to the church, so that Catholic mass was celebrated in the choir and Protestant services in the nave, separated by a dividing wall.

It was not until 1936 that an agreement was reached with the Catholic Church; the church became the property of the Protestant Church in Baden.

On the Feast of St. John in 1936, the Protestant Heiliggeist parish celebrated services in a church without a dividing wall for the first time again.

properties.name: Jesuitenkirche
properties.description:
The Jesuit Church (correct name: Pfarrkirche Heiliger Geist und St. Ignatius) is the largest and most important church in Heidelberg alongside the Heiliggeistkirche and forms the architectural focal point of the former Jesuit quarter in the old town in the immediate vicinity of Universitätsplatz. Today, it is the main church of the Roman Catholic Holy Spirit parish in Heidelberg.

In 1685, the Electoral Palatinate fell to Elector Philipp Wilhelm (1685-90) of the Catholic Palatinate-Neuburg line; he returned the Catholic Church to the Palatinate and called the Jesuits to Heidelberg. After the destruction of Heidelberg by the French in 1693, Elector Johann Wilhelm (1690-1716) wanted to turn Heidelberg into a center of Catholic activity with the help of the Jesuits. The large college building was erected between 1703 and 1711 and construction of the church began immediately afterwards. The Elector provided building land, stones from the Thick Tower of Heidelberg Castle, timber from the manorial forests, sand from the moat and free transportation. The architect Johann Adam Breunig (around 1660-1727) drew up the plan. The first phase of construction work lasted until 1723.  
Elector Johann Wilhelm died in 1716; his brother and successor Karl Philipp fought with the Reformed Church Council over the 80th question of the Heidelberg Catechism and the nave of the Heiliggeistkirche, as a result of which the Elector moved his residence and government to Mannheim in 1720. It was not until 1749 that building work could be resumed thanks to the generosity of Elector Karl Theodor (1742-1799). The nave was already covered the following year and the façade and vaulting were completed in 1751; however, the work dragged on until the late fall of 1759. The Mannheim court architect Franz Wilhelm Rabaliatti (1716-1782), who was also building the Seminarium Carolinum for the Heidelberg Jesuits, was in charge of the construction. After the dissolution of the Jesuit order in 1773, their tasks and institutions were taken over by the Lazarists from 1782 to 1793. In the following years, the church served as a military hospital; since 01.11.1809, it has been the parish church of the Catholic parish of Heilig Geist.  
The baroque interior is no longer preserved today. The altarpiece by the Kaulbach pupil Andreas Müller has been preserved. Elector Frederick the Victorious is buried in a crypt in the north-east corner of the church. To the east of the church portals is the entrance to the former Jesuit College. Originally, the Jesuit facilities included a grammar school (now the Philosophical Seminary) and the Seminarium Carolinum, which is now used by the university administration.

properties.name: Botanischer Garten Heidelberg
properties.description:
Heidelberg Botanical Garden  
Place of recreation with a "green school"

Founded in 1593, the Botanical Garden of Heidelberg University is one of the oldest botanical gardens: important scientific work by Heidelberg botanists is inextricably linked to it and its research and conservation collections are of great importance. There is also a herbarium with unique specimens. The Heidelberg Botanic Garden is a place of scientific research and academic teaching, protects endangered plant species, offers public education programs and is an important institution for the horticultural trade and its training. Last but not least, it is also a place of tranquillity and recreation. The Heidelberg Botanic Garden's Green School offers a wide range of public programs: guided tours and courses, such as "By candlelight through the tropics", or "Making your own natural cosmetics" and even children's birthday parties are on offer. There are also private guided tours on topics such as "Living fossils" or "Carnivorous plants". Offers for school classes and kindergartens impart botanical knowledge with the aim of developing enjoyment in dealing with this living world, to feel appreciation for these natural foundations of life and to motivate a willingness to treat nature with care.

properties.name: Electoral Palatinate Museum Heidelberg
properties.description:
Das Kurpfälzische Museum gehört zu den großen Kultureinrichtungen der Stadt Heidelberg.

Es versammelt einzigartige Bestände zur Historie der Kurpfalz, die viele Jahrhunderte lang zu den bedeutendsten deutschen Territorien gehörte und Weltpolitik machte, zuletzt in den Auseinandersetzungen des Dreißigjährigen Krieges und in den kriegerischen Konflikten mit Ludwig XIV. im Pfälzischen Erbfolgekrieg. Eine Fülle von Objekten vermitteln Geschichte und Lebensgeschichten. Die kostbare Sammlung Frankenthaler Porzellans und das Tafelsilber der letzten Kurfürstin Elisabeth Augusta verweisen auf den Glanz und Repräsentationswillen des Hofes, aber auch auf ein ungestörtes Wirtschaftswachstum im 18. Jh., das erst durch die Napoleonischen Kriege wieder unterbrochen wurde. Den geschichtlichen Wandel zeigt das Altersporträt der Kurfürstin, die sich als Bürgerin in dezent dunkler Kleidung präsentiert. Gemälde durchziehen wie ein roter Faden das gesamte Museum. In der Kurpfalz-Abteilung werden in Art einer Porträtgalerie die herausragenden Protagonisten der Regionalgeschichte vorgestellt, darunter der „Winterkönig“ Friedrich V. mit seiner Gemahlin Elizabeth Stuart, „Liselotte von der Pfalz“ und der Hofnarr Perkeo. Viele Jahrtausende zurück datieren die Bestände der Archäologischen Abteilung, die auf 2 Etagen präsentiert wird. Von der Altsteinzeit (homo heidelbergensis) bis in die Tage der kurpfälzischen Residenz wird die wechselvolle Geschichte Heidelbergs dokumentiert. Damit werden 600 000 Jahre Menschheitsgeschichte weit über die hiesige Region hinaus lebendig. Den weitaus größten Raum nimmt die Römerzeit ein. Versteckte Kostbarkeiten finden sich in der Graphischen Sammlung, die zu den umfangreichsten Südwestdeutschlands gehört. Mit etwa 7.000 Aquarellen und 13.000 Druckgraphiken umfasst die Sammlung Exponate vom ausgehenden Mittelalter bis ins 21. Jh.. Arbeiten regionaler Künstler sind in ihr ebenso vertreten wie herausragende Einzelblätter, zu denen Marc Chagalls „Der blaue Bär“ gehört. Sammlungsschwerpunkte liegen in den Themenbereichen Romantik, Kurpfalz, Porträts, historische Darstellungen und Flugblätter. Sie können nach vorheriger Anfrage im Vorlageraum des Kabinetts eingesehen werden.

Seit Herbst 2020 ist das Kurpfälzische Museum um eine Attraktion reicher: mit der "HD Discovery Station" reist es sich bequem und auf höchstem digitalen Niveau in die Zeit der Kelten und Römer! Mithilfe eines Spielcontrollers können die Besucher auf eine virtuelle Zeitreise gehen. Wie mit einem Gleitschirm fliegen sie über die keltische Höhensiedlung Heiligenberg oder spazieren durch die römischen Siedlungen am Neckarufer. Erfasst wurde eine Fläche von 100 Quadratkilometern, 130 000 Objekte sind bereits integriert. Das Projekt ist ausbaufähig: neueste wissenschaftliche Erkenntnisse werden von den Spezialisten der Archäologischen Abteilung des KMH unmittelbar integriert, weitere Zeitebenen sind in Vorbereitung.

properties.name: BODY WORLDS Heidelberg
properties.description:
# BODY WORLDS Museum in Heidelberg - On the trail of happiness

Great love, a carefree life, true friendship ... Everyone strives for happiness. But where does happiness live? Why can't we get enough of it? And why can't we keep happiness forever? The KÖRPERWELTEN Museum in the Altes Hallenbad explores these and other questions about happiness.

It is not only dedicated to the anatomy of humans, their organ functions and questions about health, but also the anatomy of happiness.

Gunther von Hagens and Angelina Whalley are presenting their exhibition on the human body, which was specially designed for Heidelberg, on an area of around 1000 m² in the former men's pool of the old indoor swimming pool. It is a reminder of what is our most precious asset: our own body. The aim of the exhibition is to show visitors the complexity of the human body in a lifelike way and thus sensitize them to their own body in all situations and phases of life.

The exhibition is based on Gunther von Hagens' invention of plastination. The scientist invented the preservation process back in 1977 at the University of Heidelberg and has been perfecting it ever since. His plastinates impress with their extremely precise, scientifically sound preparation as well as their creative, aesthetic and often unusual form of presentation.

More than 45 million people around the world have already been inspired and fascinated by the KÖRPERWELTEN exhibitions, 10 million of them in Germany alone. Never before has an exhibition moved the public so much and changed their view of their own physicality so lastingly as Gunther von Hagens' BODY WORLDS.

properties.name: Universitätsmuseum und Aula der Alten Universität
properties.description: The opening hours can be found on the homepage at [http://www.uni-heidelberg.de/einrichtungen/museen/](http://www.uni-heidelberg.de/einrichtungen/museen/).

properties.name: Heidelberg Zoo
properties.description:
Der Zoo Heidelberg mit wunderschönem Baumbestand ist ein beliebtes Ausflugsziel für die ganze Familie.

Auf Safari durch den Zoo: Über 160 verschiedene Tierarten aus aller Welt laden im Zoo Heidelberg zu einer spannenden Entdeckungsreise ein. Die Roten Pandas verbringen den Tag gerne hoch oben im Geäst und die Sumatra-Tiger lieben es, durch den dichten Bambuswald in ihrem Gehege zu streifen. Kaum zu übersehen sind die leuchtend orange-roten Kubaflamingos auf ihrem See oder die Asiatischen Elefanten, die sich im Sommer gerne im Badebecken abkühlen.

Ebenso wie das Berberlöwenpaar Chalid und Binta, erfreuen sich die Mähnenrobben bei den Besuchern besonderer Beliebtheit. Zweimal täglich, außer freitags, findet an der Robbenanlage eine kommentierte Fütterung mit Training statt. Zoobesucher erhalten dort viele Infos zu den Mähnenrobben und zur Arbeit der Tierpfleger. Vielfältige Aktionstage und Veranstaltungen im Zoo Heidelberg sorgen das ganze Jahr über für Abwechslung. Bei Familien mit Kindern sind das große Spielschiff „Arche“, die Klettertürme und die beiden Wasserspielplätze beliebte Zwischenstationen beim Zoobesuch.

Mit seinem didaktischen Konzept setzt der Zoo Heidelberg auf erlebnisreiche Bildung: Bei Rundgängen mit der Zooschule Heidelberg lernen Kinder sowie Erwachsene Spannendes über die Tiere im Zoo Heidelberg. Im Technik- und Ausstellungsbereich des Explo Heidelberg können wissenschaftliche Phänomene erkundet werden. Der Eintritt für die Explo-Ausstellung ist im Zooeintritt bereits enthalten.

properties.name: Deutsches Verpackungs Museum
properties.description:
The German Packaging Museum is conveniently located in Heidelberg's Old Town. Here you can see a unique collection of interesting and sometimes astonishing goods packaging in a lovingly restored "emergency church".

Located in the heart of Heidelberg's old town, the - first and only - German Packaging Museum is housed in the rooms of a former emergency church. Lovingly renovated and equipped with state-of-the-art infrastructure, the building is a real gem that is worth a visit from an architectural point of view alone.

In its rooms, the museum shows the packaging of goods as a reflection of the cultural development of our society. The diverse functions of packaging are presented as well as its historical development: packaging as the result of a creative and artistic achievement. Different exhibition areas present packaging as the result of constant change: artistic and technical innovations have influenced the design of packaging at all times.

The history of industrial goods packaging is also a history of our everyday lives in the 19th and 20th centuries. A number of packaging designs can be traced back to important artists of their time, are real "works of art" and are not just collector's items, but have long been a recognized part of art and design history.

Technical innovation has always had a new face over the past hundred years. The German Packaging Museum therefore also shows those "milestones" that impressively illustrate the varieties of human imagination and creativity through unusual or inventive packaging solutions, and reviews the past with brands that are still popular today.

properties.name: Prinzhorn Collection
properties.description:
The Prinzhorn Collection is a museum for art by people with exceptional mental experiences. Its well-known historical collection comprises around 6,000 works created by inmates of psychiatric institutions between 1840 and 1945.  

This globally unique collection was largely compiled by the art historian and psychiatrist Hans Prinzhorn (1886-1933) during his time as an assistant doctor at the Psychiatric Clinic of Heidelberg University. The best-known artists/authors in the historical collection include Else Blankenhorn, Franz Karl Bühler, Karl Genzel, Paul Goesch, Emma Hauck, August Klett, August Natterer, Agnes Richter, Joseph Schneller, Barbara Suckfüll and Adolf Wölfli.

**The history of the collection**

In 1919-21, Hans Prinzhorn wrote letters to psychiatric clinics in German-speaking countries with the then clinic director Karl Wilmanns, requesting artistic patient works for the establishment of a museum for psychopathological art.

In 1922, Prinzhorn published his richly illustrated study "Bildnerei der Geisteskranken" based on the collection, which appealed to many art lovers and artists of his time and became the surrealists' pictorial bible. Reprinted several times and translated into various languages, the book remains a classic.

In 1938, clinic director Carl Schneider donated works from the collection to the traveling exhibition "Degenerate Art". In the exhibition, they are misused as pathological comparative material for modern art.

Forgotten after the war, the collection was rediscovered by Harald Szeemann in 1963. He shows a selection at the Kunsthalle Bern. National and international exhibitions followed, making the collection famous once again.

In 2001, the collection finally receives its own museum building, a converted old neurology lecture hall on the grounds of the old university hospital in Heidelberg.

**The collection today**

Since 1980, the collection has been growing again through art by psychiatric patients. This newer collection now comprises around 20,000 works. These include works by Friedrich Boss, Gudrun Biersky, Vanda Vieira-Schmidt, Sonja Gerstner, Alfred Stief and Dietrich Orth. In order to be able to regularly present new acquisitions and a permanent exhibition alongside the temporary exhibitions in the future, an extension is planned.

**The Prinzhorn Collection Museum - Exhibitions and Research**

The museum presents three to four themed exhibitions each year. The aim of the museum is to help destigmatize mental illness. By contextualizing and interpreting artistic works that are shaped by exceptional mental experiences and their social consequences, it contributes to the inclusion of affected people. As part of Heidelberg University Hospital, the museum sees itself not only as a museum and exhibition venue, but also as a scientific institution that researches the fate of the artists represented here, their works and overarching issues. For this reason, scientists, artists and other interested parties can view the museum's archive and depot holdings by appointment. The museum's academic staff will be happy to provide information and assistance.

properties.name: Old Town Heidelberg
properties.description:
With its romantic alleyways, quaint traditional restaurants, and historic buildings, the Old Town is considered the heart and historic center of Heidelberg.

It is world-famous for its unique triad of city, mountains, and river. Around 10,000 Heidelberg residents live in the old town and, like visitors, appreciate the short distances, the multitude of [cultural and leisure facilities](https://www.heidelberg-marketing.de/culture), the attractive [shopping opportunities](https://www.heidelberg-marketing.de/entdecken/shopping "shopping opportunities") and the extensive [range of restaurants and hotels](https://www.heidelberg-marketing.de/planen/uebernachten "range of restaurants and hotels"). In addition, the old town is the founding seat of Germany's oldest university, the "Ruperto Carola." Students from near and far attend Heidelberg University, giving the old town its lively, youthful, and international flair.

The old town covers around 1,380 hectares, of which only 9.8 percent is built up. The district is characterized by the forest area of the Königstuhl, which at 564 meters is one of the highest mountains in the Odenwald.

**Highlights:** [Castle](https://www.heidelberg-marketing.de/poi/schloss-heidelberg)

[Mountain railway](https://www.heidelberg-marketing.de/poi/heidelberger-bergbahnen) [Market square](https://www.heidelberg-marketing.de/poi/marktplatz) [University library](https://www.heidelberg-marketing.de/poi/universitaetsbibliothek)

[Main street](https://www.heidelberg-marketing.de/poi/hauptstrasse) [Old bridge](https://www.heidelberg-marketing.de/poi/alte-bruecke) [Grain market](https://www.heidelberg-marketing.de/poi/kornmarkt)

Lower Street [Theater](https://www.heidelberg-marketing.de/poi/theater-und-orchester-heidelberg) [University Square](https://www.heidelberg-marketing.de/poi/universitaetsplatz) [Karlstor Gate](https://www.heidelberg-marketing.de/poi/karlstor)

Schnelldorf, das "Wanderparadies der Frankenhöhe", liegt in einem Mittelgebirge, das bis zu 550m über NN ansteigt. Die Höhenzüge sind mit ausgedehnten Mischwäldern bestanden. Weite Talauen, durchzogen von kleinen Flüssen und Bächen und durchsetzt mit zahlreichen Seen und Teichen, umgeben den Ort. Sehenswürdigkeiten: St. Georgs-Kirche im OT Oberampfrach (bedeutender Flügelaltar; an der Empore sind zeitgenössische Bürger- und Bauernportraits), St. Jakobs-Kirche im OT Wildenholz (Reste wertvoller Fresken). Freizeitangebot: Markierte Wanderwege, Tennis, Angeln, Reiten, verschiedene kleine Badeseen, Spielplätze, Kegelbahn. Bahnhaltestation Strecke Stuttgart/Nürnberg

properties.description: The market square is centrally located in Rothenburg ob der Tauber, directly in front of the historic town hall.

properties.name: Trochtelfingen local history room
properties.description:
The former town hall in Trochtelfingen is now home to the Heimatstuben.

Lovingly furnished rooms with original items have been open to visitors on request since 1999.

The exhibition rooms focus on farming and rural lifestyles of the 19th and early 20th centuries, inviting visitors to linger and marvel.

Projector, DVD player, CD player, internet access (WLAN), screen, flipchart, pin board, presentation case

Billiards, table tennis, studio, children's playroom, music corner, weir tower, sunbathing lawn, sun terrace, children's playground, play area, campfire site, volleyball court, bike hire and lockable bike room, sauna and relaxation area.

properties.name: Ladestation Hotel Dietz
properties.description:
With us in the Ostalb, you can collect impressive tour kilometers and altitude meters thanks to e-bikes. Our hotel in Bopfingen is an ideal starting point for e-bike tours.

We offer free charging stations for our guests. We have two lockable garages for up to 10 bikes.

As an additional service, we have bike maps, information and special offers ready for you and will be happy to advise you.

The Hotel Dietz is a friendly, personal hotel that is individually furnished and family-run.

properties.name: Castle garden Rothenburg ob der Tauber
properties.description:
Die Wege führen vorbei an alten Bäumen, Blumenrabatten erfreuen das Auge. Bänke laden zum Ausruhen ein und die Ausblicke auf das Taubertal und die Stadtkulisse sind herrlich.  

Das Gelände ist Standort der durch ein Erdbeben im Jahre 1356 zerstörten Reichsburg der Hohenstaufen.

properties.name: Oberelchingen monastery garden
properties.description: Ein Ort der Ruhe und Meditation ist der Klostergarten Oberelchingen. Typische Pflanzen eines mittelalterlichen Klostergartens sind ebenso zu finden wie moderne Heilpflanzen.Von der Plattform ergibt sich ein weiter Blick auf das grüne Band des Donautals. Zur Andacht lädt der Prozessionsweg ("Sieben-Schmerzen-Weg") mit Bronzeskulpturen und Meditationstexten ein.

TimeBike rents out trekking and full-mountain eBikes for both day trips and longer tours.

properties.name: New Gallery Calw
properties.description:
STEINBLICKE + Nature Depictions, Wolfgang Binder

SELF-DISCOVERY THROUGH FORMS AND COLORS, Natalia Kairies  

The Neue Galerie Calw was opened on June 24, 2022, by two artists from Calw. Natalia Kairies' artistic work is diverse. It includes extraordinary clay works and various painting techniques in acrylic, cement, and clay. Wolfgang Binder presents 38 stone views. Strictly limited photographs and prints offer fascinating insights into the rock. What at first glance looks like abstract art is actually the image of compositions of mineral and biogenic components created by nature. The variety of motifs and the richness of structures, shapes, and colors are surprising. Let yourself be inspired by the incredible artistic power of nature. Commissioned works are welcome. Arrangements for opening the gallery and inquiries can be made with Natalia Kairies at 07051 1597690 or Wolfgang Binder at 0170 184 6680.

properties.name: Breig´s Motorrad- und Spielzeugmuseum
properties.description:
Walter Breig’s museum in Zell am Harmersbach is a true feast for the eyes of any motorcycle fan. Mobility, combined with sportiness, creativity, idealism, and passion—that’s what his motorcycle and toy museum has stood for since its opening on May 1, 2015.

Spanning over 900 square meters, the museum presents a unique comprehensive exhibition of many milestones in motorcycle history in a light-filled hall. This permanent exhibition features over 80 historically significant original vehicles from the past nine decades. From Adler, BMW, and Kreidler to NSU and Zündapp, visitors can experience the spirit of the times in motorized two-wheelers up close, making every motorcyclist’s and collector’s heart beat faster.


Walter Breig, a passionate collector of time-honored two-wheeled machines for 60 years, tinkerer, and gifted restorer, is the initiator and driving force behind this impressive exhibition of roadworthy motorcycles and “firehorses” gleaming with chrome and paint—all masterfully and lovingly restored by Walter Breig himself.


And—take note!—the museum opens up a second exciting dimension with its magnificent collection of tin toys: over 2,000 exhibits are displayed in more than 80 man-sized display cases, offering an overview of the cultural history of toys: Toy cars, motorcycles, carriages, and, of course, the good old train—a true delight for children and adults alike.


Why and how does such a large private collection come to be? Ask Mr. Breig yourself during your visit; he’ll be happy to answer your questions and will gladly show you his “favorite exhibits.”

Step into a world full of wonder and imagination, let yourself be transported back in time, and join us on a journey through the ages.


There’s no art without a patron: Erwin Junker, owner of the Maschinen Fabrik in Nordrach and proprietor of the museum hall, is a dedicated supporter and benefactor working behind the scenes, providing Walter Breig with advice and assistance in all matters—a driving force behind the new museum.

properties.name: Viewing platform on the "Druckele"
properties.description:
The Lehberg near Gaildorf attracts visitors with the “Druckele” and a modern observation deck. Nestled along the “FeenSpuren” premium hiking trail, the deck offers hikers fascinating views across the Kocher Valley all the way to the Hohenlohe Plain.

Lehberg and “Druckele”

To the west of Gaildorf lies the Lehberg, a striking spur of the Limpurger Mountains. Together with the neighboring Kirgel, it forms a forested ridge that serves as a local recreation area for the region. The highest point of this ridge is known locally as “Druckele.” It is precisely at this exposed spot that a special attraction for nature lovers is located: an architecturally striking wooden viewing platform.

Best View

The structure was built as part of efforts to enhance the region’s appeal to tourists and blends harmoniously into the forest landscape. From the platform, a sweeping panoramic view opens up to the north. The view sweeps across the deeply incised Kochertal valley and the “Westheimer Pforte,” and on clear days extends across the Hohenlohe Plain all the way to the Einkorn near Schwäbisch Hall.

Premium Hiking

The Druckele is accessible via the certified premium hiking trail “FeenSpuren – Kirgel Ausblicke.” The approximately 6.4-kilometer loop trail follows nature trails that pass directly by the platform. Nearby are the Kernerturm tower and the barbecue area and playground at Kirgel, making the Lehberg a versatile destination in the Limpurger Land region.

properties.name: AliSa adventure trail Wolfslochrunde
properties.description:
Start at the hiking parking lot. This can be found by car when driving on the B292 from Helmstadt to Waibstadt, shortly after Helmstadt on the right-hand side.

There are two concrete field paths leading off from here, please take the one on the right. Then it goes past fields, along the Auerbach and after approx. 300 m you cross a bridge.


Continue along the concreted field path until you finally reach the edge of the Forlewald forest.

This is the first highlight of the route. The small pond is a water conservation area, but there is still plenty to discover here (please follow the signs around the pond).

Pass the pond on the left. You are now on a beautiful forest path with lots to discover.  
At first you will pass the Wolfslochhütte hut on a slight uphill section, then continue through the forest. After a short stretch, you reach the Wolfslocheiche oak tree.

On reaching the mountain, turn right onto the forest path and then right again after a short distance at the crossroads.

Now it's always slightly downhill.

Here you will discover some ant hills - some are even fenced in.

Continue towards the Alfred-Winterbauer beech tree.

Following the path further downhill, you reach the Wolfsloch beech. In spring 2020, the beech was still in full sap, but unfortunately it has since died off.

Finally, you come back to the pond.  
From here, the same concreted field path leads back to the hiking parking lot.

properties.name: Schillergarten
properties.description:
From a cemetery to a green oasis amid the hustle and bustle of traffic: Gaildorf’s Schillergarten holds a fascinating history.

Today’s Schillergarten combines church history with the legacy of a world-renowned poet. Where a small green space now defies the street noise, the town’s first cemetery stood from 1710 to 1906. At the time of its establishment, the site was still located a short distance outside the gates of the town center itself, to allow room for the town’s growth. A massive stone cemetery wall completely enclosed the consecrated grounds, clearly demarcating the resting place of the dead.

The history of burials in Gaildorf, however, goes back even further. Originally, the town’s deceased were buried in what is now the district of Münster. For a long time, the parish church responsible for Gaildorf was located in Münster. It was not until 1433 that Gaildorf itself became an independent parish. Nevertheless, the citizens did not abandon their burial site in Münster, so burials continued to take place there. It was not until 1710 that the cemetery was moved to Gaildorf.

After the new cemetery opened in December 1906, the old site was decommissioned. The cemetery owes its current name to the famous Schiller family of poets. Karl von Schiller, Friedrich Schiller’s eldest son, worked as a district forester at the nearby Reichenberg Castle in the 1820s. He fell in love with Louise Friederike Locher, the daughter of Gaildorf’s chief medical officer. On February 12, 1825, the couple married in Gaildorf. On the 100th anniversary of the poet’s death in 1905, a Schiller monument was erected on what was then the cemetery grounds.

To this day, fragments of the old cemetery wall, scattered gravestones, and a stone statue of Christ dating back some 140 years serve as reminders of the site’s sacred past.

properties.name: Rothenburg ob der Tauber
properties.description:
No matter how or from where you approach the city, the mighty city wall magically draws you in and promises a different world behind the gates.  
Curious, you enter and soon discover that your feelings and premonitions were not wrong.  
The painters and writers of the Romantic period who were drawn to Rothenburg felt the same way much earlier. "I thought I had suddenly been transported to the Middle Ages", wrote Ludwig Richter in his memoirs around 150 years ago, and one involuntarily searches the streets for the motifs that could have inspired Karl Spitzweg's famous paintings.

The old town of Rothenburg ob der Tauber is one of the "particularly landscape-defining monuments" in Bavaria. The Bavarian State Office for the Preservation of Monuments only classifies a few very special places. In Romantic Franconia, the old towns of Bad Windheim and Dinkelsbühl, Schillingsfürst Castle and the Hesselberg have a particularly large number of these monuments.

[More information](http://www.romantisches-franken.de/Staedte)

properties.name: Wünsch Lake
properties.description:
Nestled among large old trees lies a small, dreamy lake, divided in two by a bridge. In the northern part, swimmers get their money’s worth. The broad bathing cove creates a holiday feeling. South of the bridge, the diving area beckons. In this area there are three springs that provide slightly cooler and wonderfully clear water.

**Facilities:** large sunbathing lawn, picnic benches and tables, restaurant with beer garden

properties.name: Schäfertanz-Kabinett (Shepherd dance cabinet)
properties.description: The Rothenburg brotherhood of shepherds has met annually since 1472 for the Shepherds' Day with a church service and feast. The young shepherds danced with the citizens' daughters. The exhibition in the gatehouse of St Wolfgang's Church (15th century) documents shepherding in the Rothenburg area and the custom of this joyful dance, which was revived at a carnival event in 1911

properties.name: Mittelalterliches Kriminalmuseum
properties.description: Over 1000 years of legal history on an exhibition area of around 3000 m²: the Mittelalterliches Kriminalmuseum (Medieval Crime Museum) houses an important collection of legal history. In addition to instruments of torture and devices for the execution of corporal, life and honour punishments, the museum also exhibits valuable paintings, prints, engravings, seals and law books. The most prominent exhibits are the so-called Iron Maiden of Nuremberg, which Bram Stoker also adapted into literature, and replicas of the imperial insignia.

properties.name: Toppler-Schlösschen (Toppler Castle)
properties.description: The picturesque Toppler-Schlösschen (Toppler-Schlösschen) is somehow reminiscent of an oversized birdhouse: the small moated castle, built in 1388/89 for the then mayor Heinrich Toppler, is part defence tower, part residential building. The fully preserved building is furnished with furniture from the 16th to the 19th century.

properties.name: Burggarten Rothenburg ob der Tauber
properties.description:
The beautifully landscaped Castle Garden, with its geometric garden layout from the 17th/18th century and 8 sandstone figures representing the four seasons and the four elements, is well worth a visit. From here you have a wonderful view over the southern part of the town, of the Double Bridge and Kobolzell Church toward the Tauber Valley, as well as of Toppler Castle, built in 1388.

The site is the location of the Imperial Castle of the Hohenstaufen, which was destroyed by an earthquake in 1356.

properties.name: St. John's Church Rothenburg ob der Tauber

Das Baudenkmal aus dem Jahre 1270 beherbergte über sieben Jahrhunderte verschiedenste Handwerker. Die Ausstellung führt Wohn- und Arbeitsmilieu vergangener Zeiten eindrücklich vor Augen.

properties.name: RothenburgMuseum
properties.description: Here you can learn all about the eventful history of the former imperial city of Rothenburg, highlight: monastery kitchen from the 13th century

properties.name: Bayerisches Schulmuseum (Bavarian School Museum)
properties.description: How and what did the first humans learn? Have there always been exercise books? What did lessons look like 100 years ago? The Bayerisches Schulmuseum (Bavarian School Museum) presents the history of learning and teaching from the Stone Age to the present in a vivid and entertaining way. For example, in the "Schreibstube", which is dedicated to the development of writing. Here you can write on Egyptian papyrus, scratch on wax tablets and try out letterpress printing with lead type. In the historical classroom from 1920, today's school classes can experience the strict discipline of past generations of pupils. Another section provides insights into the Jewish school system in Bavaria from the early 19th century to the present day.

properties.name: Lauschtour "Through the Leipheim Moor"
properties.description:
...interessant, humorvoll und überraschend.

**HINWEIS: Aus Sicherheitsgründen ist der Bohlenweg momentan nicht begehbar. Die Lauschtour kann mit einer kleinen Streckenänderung jedoch durchgeführt werden.**

Schwarzer Torf und tiefe Tümpel: Erkunden Sie hier eine der mystischsten Landschaften in Bayerisch-Schwaben. Hier hören Sie den Pulsschlag eines wiederbewässerten Moors! Der Biologe erklärt faszinierende Naturphänomene. Außerdem gibt’s Interviews mit ehemaligen Torfstechern und wir schauen bei einer Straußenfarm vorbei. Das pickt!

**Infos zur Strecke**

Streckenlänge: 4,2 km

Schwierigkeit: leicht

Gehzeit: ca. 2 Stunden - ab Lauschpunkt 4 befinden Sie sich im Naturschutzgebiet. Bitte verlassen Sie die Wege nicht und nehmen Sie Rücksicht auf Tiere und Pflanzen.


**Mit App oder iPod auf Tour:**

Smartphone-Besitzer nutzen einfach unsere kostenlose Lauschtour-App.

Alles, was Sie brauchen, sind Smartphone-Kopfhörer oder die Lautsprecher-Funktion und etwas Zeit und Muse zum Wandern oder Radeln. Und schon eröffnet sich Ihnen ganz großes Kino für die Ohren mit reizvollen, unkonventionell gestalteten Audio-Beiträgen.

Und so funktioniert`s:

**1. App laden**

Kostenlos im App Store und im Google Play Store unter „Bayerisch-Schwaben-Lauschtour“. iPods gibt es auch zum Ausleihen. (mehr hierzu im Internet)

**2. App starten**

**3. Loslauschen**

Starten Sie Ihre Tour zu Fuß (oder ggfls. per Fahrrad). Von Lauschpunkt zu Lauschpunkt erwarten Sie spannende Audio- Erlebnisse – fantasievoll vertont und journalistisch recherchiert.

**Tipp:** Laden Sie die App bereits vor Ihrem Start zur Lauschtour und speichern sie diese offline ab – so sind Sie unabhängig von der Verbindungsleistung.

Danke, dass Sie die Einzigartigkeit der Natur bewahren und stets auf den Wegen bleiben, keinen Müll hinterlassen und auf Lärm verzichten.

properties.name: Lauschtour "Keltenpfad Ichenhausen"
properties.description:
**Current notice: Lauschpunkt 6 marked on the maps is currently not accessible. The audio tour ends at the Celtic farmstead (Lauschpunkt 5), where you can now get even more detailed information.**

The most famous Celts are called Asterix and Obelix — because the term Celts comes from the Latin CELTAE or GALLI. Although the little Gaulish village was not located in the family and children’s region, you can also follow in the footsteps of the Celts in the Günzburg district.

At 6 listening points — starting from the parking lot at the cemetery in Ichenhausen — the lives of the Celts and druids are presented acoustically.

Set off on an exciting search for clues, past burial mounds, sacred trees, and a nearly vanished fortification in the forest. The highlight of the tour: the lovingly reconstructed Celtic farmstead.


You can enjoy the listening experience in the open air in two ways:

Via the app, which is available free of charge in the App Store and Google Play Store under “Bayerisch-Schwaben-Lauschtour,” or via iPod, which can be borrowed from the Bavarian School Museum.


**Route length**: 3 km from the first to the last listening point

**Difficulty:** easy

**Walking time:** approx. 35 minutes (one way)


**iPod rental station**: Bavarian School Museum Ichenhausen, Schlossplatz 3-5, 89335 Ichenhausen, Tel. 08223/6189

properties.name: Old guard Haiger
properties.description:
The guardhouse was located in front of the then still standing city wall and was built in 1810 in the Greek temple style. It served the town guard as a guardroom and detention cell. Carters passing through had to pay "road and lake tolls" there. During this period Haiger belonged to the Duchy of Berg ("French period") and was effectively under Napoleon's rule. After Haiger became part of Nassau again, the small guardhouse lost its function and was put up for auction as early as 1817. After 1827, the town wall was also gradually dismantled.

Next to the watchtower was one of the public fountains, which gave its name to the inn opposite. Not far from the Wacht in Hickenweg is the site of the so-called "Wilhelmshof".

Hickenweg (also called Hofhausweg) used to be the main road to Langenaubach, to the Hickengrund and to the Westerwald.

The Westerwald road was not built until 1823/24.

properties.name: Bürgerbrunnen Fountain
properties.description:
De Bürgerbrunnen, een bronzen beeld van de Osnabrücker beeldhouwer Hans Gerd Ruwe (1926-1995), staat sinds 1986 op de Platz des Westfälischen Friedens. Ruwe ontwierp ook andere fonteinen en sculpturen in de stad, zoals de "Steckenpferdreiter-Brunnen" bij de St. Catharinakerk, "die Waschfrau" bij Vitihof of "das Tiergericht" bij de dierentuin.  
De burgerfontein werd in 1980 door de burgers van Osnabrück geschonken ter gelegenheid van het 1200-jarig bestaan van de stad. Het brons, dat uit 1200 afzonderlijke delen bestaat, werd besteld bij Ruwe. De fontein symboliseert de geschiedenis van Osnabrück door middel van verschillende landschappelijke motieven. Zelfs hun oriëntatie heeft een overeenkomstige betekenis: alle figuren die naar het stadhuis leunen, staan voor positieve gebeurtenissen. Figuren die in de tegenovergestelde richting wijzen, staan voor negatieve gebeurtenissen uit de geschiedenis van de stad. De fontein bestaat ook uit drie schalen. De grootste kom stelt het verleden voor. De stadsgeschiedenis van Osnabrück stroomt er in de vorm van water doorheen. Zijn grootte verwijst naar de bestaande kennis van het verleden. Het water stroomt verder in de middelste schaal, die het heden voorstelt. Het is verbonden met het verleden doordat de huidige gebeurtenissen in het verleden overgaan. De kleinste kom symboliseert de toekomst. Het staat onder invloed van het heden. De onderlinge verbinding wordt gezien als een herinnering: het verleden beïnvloedt het heden en het heden beïnvloedt de toekomst.  
De fontein was oorspronkelijk bedoeld voor de markt, vandaar dat sommige figuren, zoals Barbarossa en Hendrik de Leeuw, er ook naar neigen.  

## Selectie van afzonderlijke motieven  
De keizer Frederik I Barbarossa (Italiaans voor Roodbaard) rijst op uit de top van de fontein. Hij verleende Osnabrück in 1171 stadsrechten en een eigen rechtsgebied. De leeuw in de grote kom staat voor de tegenstander van de keizer, de Gelderse hertog Hendrik de Leeuw. Deze zorgde voor een eigen jurisdictie in het gebied van het domkapittel om zich niet aan de stad te hoeven onderwerpen.  
In 1488 eiste de meester-kleermaker Johann Lenethun de afschaffing van de privileges van de raad en de geestelijkheid. Er volgde een opstand met plunderingen in de stad. Op 25 mei 1490 werd Lenethun door Osnabrücker soldaten gegrepen en nog dezelfde dag op de markt terechtgesteld, waarmee de opstand eindigde. Deze scène vormt een ander motief.  
De heksenvervolging in de 16e en 17e eeuw wordt gesymboliseerd door een vrouw op de brandstapel, terwijl een ander beeld de Dood is die met zijn zeis door de menigte maait en duidelijk maakt dat iedereen voor hem gelijk is en dat hij geen onderscheid maakt tussen arm en rijk. De "zwarte dood", zoals de pest ook wel werd genoemd, trof Osnabrück meerdere malen: in 1350, 1575-1577 en 1599. Alleen al tijdens de laatste twee epidemieën stierven meer dan 4000 mensen aan de pest.  
Een ander motief is de vredesruiter. Hij stelt de boodschappers voor die tijdens de onderhandelingen over de Vrede van Westfalen tussen Münster en Osnabrück reisden, voordat de vrede uiteindelijk op 25 oktober 1648 vanaf de trappen van het stadhuis van Osnabrück kon worden afgekondigd.  
Als verbindend element stroomt de stadsrivier van Osnabrück, de Hase, over de hele fontein. Zij beschermt de stad, maar bergt ook gevaren in zich, zoals de mogelijkheid om in haar wateren te verdrinken.

properties.name: Gedenkteken oude synagoge
properties.description:
In de "Alte-Synagoge-Straße" herdenkt het monument "Alte Synagoge" (Oude Synagoge) het gebedshuis dat in de pogromnacht van 9 op 10 november 1938 door de nationaal-socialisten werd verwoest. Een gebroken davidster symboliseert het vernietigde Joodse leven. Vier panelen tonen de stadia van uitsluiting en ontrechting, vervolging, deportatie en moord op de Osnabrücker joden. 162 hekpalen herdenken 162 vermoorde mensen.

## Bouw van de synagoge

Nadat de joodse gemeenschap van Osnabrück sinds 1872 het huis aan het Barfüßerkloster 6/7 als synagoge en schoolgebouw had gebruikt, werd op 12 september 1905 de eerste steen gelegd voor een nieuw gebouw aan de Rolandstraße 3-5 (de huidige "Alte-Synagoge-Straße"). Het gebouw met meerdere verdiepingen en een indrukwekkende koepel werd gebouwd door de Keulse architect Sigmund Münchhausen in neogotische stijl en bood plaats aan de ongeveer 450 leden van de congregatie. De plechtige opening vond plaats op 13 september 1906. Het aangrenzende bijgebouw diende als gemeenschapscentrum en bood onderdak aan een eenklassige school. Een inzicht in de oude synagoge biedt het schilderij "De twee joden" van de Osnabrücker schilder Felix Nussbaum uit 1926, dat in het Felix Nussbaum Huis te zien is en de kunstenaar naast de voorzanger van de joodse gemeente toont tegen de achtergrond van het interieur van de synagoge. Het dubbelportret wordt beschouwd als een verklaring van Nussbaums geloof in het joodse geloof.

## Vernietiging van de synagoge en achtergrond

In de Reichspogromnacht van 1938 werd de synagoge van Osnabrück ontwijd, geplunderd en vervolgens in brand gestoken door SA-troepen. Op de dag van de brandstichting gaf burgemeester Erich Gaertner opdracht het slechts beschadigde massieve gebouw om "bouwpolitieke redenen" af te breken. Deze sloop was al achter de schermen geregeld. De Gestapo, die gevestigd was in de westelijke vleugel van Schloss Osnabrück, wilde uitbreiden, terwijl Erich Gaertner het beoogde gebied wilde inrichten als kasteelpark. Om dit mogelijk te maken bood hij de Gestapo het terrein van de synagoge aan, waarmee alle partijen instemden. De economische benarde situatie van de Joodse gemeenschap werd uitgebuit. Door discriminatie en vlucht nam de omvang van de gemeenschap vanaf 1936 drastisch af. 90 van hen werden op de dag van de pogromnacht opgesloten in de Gestapo-kelder van kasteel Osnabrück en enkele dagen later gedeporteerd naar concentratiekamp Buchenwald. Nadat de synagoge was afgebroken, werd deze wegens de financiële lasten geveild. De Stadtsparkasse (Stadsspaarbank) kocht het nu leegstaande terrein met bijgebouwen voor veel minder dan de waarde, en droeg het kort daarna over aan de stad in ruil voor een onkostenvergoeding. De stad ruilde het terrein vervolgens tegen het terrein bij het kasteel. De Gestapo bouwde echter geen nieuw gebouw.

## Geschiedenis van de synagoge na de Tweede Wereldoorlog en verdere ontwikkeling

Na 1945 kreeg de Joodse gemeenschap het gebied van de oude synagoge voorlopig terug "tot de definitieve eigendomsoverdracht". Het bijgebouw werd gebruikt als gebeds- en woongebouw. In 1949 verzocht de gemeente om officiële herbestemming, maar in 1954 kocht de overheid het gebied van de Joodse Trustmaatschappij en voegde vervolgens een bijgebouw toe aan het overheidsgebouw.

In de periode 1967-1969 werd vervolgens in de Weststadt in de straat "In der Barlage" een nieuwe synagoge met buurthuis en flats gebouwd. Vanwege het groeiende aantal leden van de gemeente, mede door een toestroom van mensen uit de voormalige Sovjet-Unie, werd besloten het buurthuis te verbouwen. Deze verbouwing begon in oktober 2008 en eindigde met de ceremoniële opening op 03 februari 2010.

properties.name: Hasestollen
properties.description:
Der Stollen verband ab 1856 den Bergbau im Norden des Piesbergs mit dem unteren Areal im Süden des Berges, auf dem im Jahr darauf der neu errichtete Zechenbahnhof in Betrieb genommen wurde.  

Der Hasestollen diente nicht nur der Kohleförderung. Auch das Grubenwasser der gesamten Zeche führte man hier in einer Wassersaige zum Fluss Hase ab. Doch das salzige Wasser führte zu erheblichen Umweltproblemen, so dass die Zeche bereits 1898 geschlossen wurde. Danach nutzte man den Hasestollen im Zweiten Weltkrieg noch einmal als Luftschutzstollen.  

Das Museum Industriekultur Osnabrück ließ den Stollen ab 1997 freilegen und eröffnete im September 2000 einen Teil des Schachtes und einen ca. 300 m langen begehbaren Stollen. Er führt vom Haseschachtgebäude, in dem sich die Dauerausstellung befindet, zu Magazin (Sonderausstellungen) und Pferdestall (Museumspädagogik) sowie zu weiteren Museumsgebäuden.

properties.name: Ondergrondse zoutwatergang in de concerttuin van Bad Rothenfelde
properties.description:
Keiner weiß genau, wie weit verzweigt das Netz der unterirdischen Solegänge ist. Fest steht, der erste Gang wurde schon 1725 aus dem Gestein gesprengt und später durch ein mannshohes Gewölbe überdacht. Dieses Gangsystem ist noch heute vorhanden und noch immer fließt die Quellsole unterirdisch von den Quellen zu den Gradierwerken. Über fast zwei Jahrhunderte fanden diese Solegänge kaum Beachtung. Das hat sich jetzt geändert.

Vom Konzertgarten führen 14 Stufen in die angenehm kühle Unterwelt von Bad Rothenfelde. 50 m des ersten historischen Solegangs sind trockenen Fußes über Holzstege und Gitterroste begehbar. Darunter fließt rostbraunes Kolkwasser, das anno dazumal ein unterirdisches Wasserrad und damit Pumpenanlagen angetrieben hat.  
Das fast mystische Erlebnis im Gewölbe wird kombiniert mit der Besichtigung der Alten Quelle im Konzertgarten. Dort wird mit einem ordentlichen Knall die historische Pumpenanlage in Bewegung gesetzt. Das ist alles nur Show, denn die Quelle von 1724 fördert nichts mehr.  

Jeden Samstag und Sonntag erwartet der Gästeführer zwischen 15:00 und 17:00 Uhr im 30 Minuten-Takt die Besucher am Eingang der Alten Quelle und spaziert anschließend ca. 50 m weiter zum Solegang.

properties.name: Aussichtsturm Ottoshöhe
properties.description:
Seit mehr als 100 Jahren ist der „Aussichtsturm Ottoshöhe” auf der Eickener Egge ein beliebtes Ausflugsziel in den Meller Bergen.

Heute trifft man dort oben, von weither sichtbar, die 4. Turmgeneration an. Der erste Aussichtsturm stammt aus dem Jahr 1895. Im Jahre 2005 wurde man auf kaum zu reparierende Schäden an der Konstruktion des 3. Turmes aufmerksam.  
Ein Fachgutachten bestätigte die Befürchtungen, dass der Aussichtsturm noch maximal bis Ende 2007 betrieben werden konnte. In sehr kurzer Zeit konnte die erforderliche  
Bausumme zusammengetragen werden. Schon im Herbst 2007 wurde der alte Turm abgebrochen und die neue „Ottoshöhe“ bereits am 14. Juni 2008 eingeweiht. Der  
Name „Ottoshöhe“ ist eine Reverenz an den 1895 amtierenden Landrat Otto von Pestel. Er war Mitbegründer des Vereins, der den Turm betreut, und stellte als Besitzer des  
Gutes Bruche das Grundstück zur Verfügung. Die besonderen Merkmale des heutigen Aussichtsturmes sind die sieben kerzengerade gewachsenen, 30 Meter langen Douglasienstämme  
als tragende Konstruktion, die nicht einmal einen Kilometer vom Standort des Turmes in den Forsten des Gutes Ostenwalde gewachsen sind. Der Weg zur Ottoshöhe  
ist von allen Himmelsrichtungen aus beschildert. Besucher können den Turm nur zu Fuß erreichen. Als Spaziergang vom Waldrand bis zum Turm sollte man etwa 20 Minuten  
einplanen.

properties.name: Söltjerbrunnen
properties.description: De fontein Söltjerbrunnen in de Marktstraße, gemaakt door beeldhouwer Bernd Maro in 1987, toont twee zoutwerkers voor de kokende pan. De ene schraapt het gekristalliseerde zout bij elkaar om het te drogen. De tweede figuur symboliseert een zoutdrager die het verkoopklare zout in zijn fietstas naar de klanten brengt. Vanwege de intense hitte voor de kokende pan en het zoutstof, dat de huid aantast, waren de zoutzieders gekleed in ruwe gewaden met capuchons. De eerste gedocumenteerde vermelding van zoutwinning in Bad Münder dateert uit 1033. Aanvankelijk begon de zoutwinning met het eenvoudig koken van het zoute bronwater in keramische of loden pannen. Vanaf 1820 werd het graduatieproces ook in Bad Münder gebruikt.

properties.name: Brunnen "Hoppenmarkt"
properties.description:
Following a design by master builder Gottfried Kastl, sculptor Bernd Maro created a semi-circular fountain made of sandstone.  

The accompanying scene "Girls and animals" is made of bronze and looks very lifelike.  

A herding girl is depicted in an idealized form and devotedly cares for domestic animals.  

The hop tendrils on the bronze column of the fountain symbolize that there were numerous citizens in the town with brewing rights and refer to the hop trade.

The rural scene is intended to remind us that there were broad sections of the population in Münder, such as craftsmen, day labourers and cottagers, who sometimes did not own land.  

Their small livestock of chickens, ducks, geese, goats and pigs - rarely cows - ensured their modest existence.  

A clear social differentiation can be seen in the distribution of livestock and land ownership (see Kornhus property) within the population.  

The well was inaugurated in November 1990.

properties.name: Adam und Eva
properties.description:
Op de noordelijke bocht van de Ith aan de Coppenbrügger kant staan twee opvallende rotsen die "Adam en Eva" worden genoemd.

Eindeloos lang geleden, aan het begin van de wereld, wilde de Schepper de aarde bezielen met goddelijke wezens. Zo ontstonden uit zijn wil een mannelijk en een vrouwelijk wezen. Hij schiep Adam, de man van de aarde, uit lichte en donkere, stevige en losse, vruchtbare en magere aarde, gecombineerd met de meest uiteenlopende zouten en sappen van de bodem. Net als hij voegde hij een partner toe aan de man, Eva, de levengeefster, omdat God wilde dat deze generatie zich zou vermenigvuldigen en de aarde vruchtbaar zou bevolken. Maar voordat God hun de bezielende adem had ingeblazen, voordat beiden levend uit de aarde konden opstaan, besloop de Boze hen en blies zijn giftige adem in. De Schepper zag dat zijn werk was bezoedeld en besefte dat het onmetelijke kwaad zou gebeuren als zijn twee schepselen zouden blijven leven. Een oneindige droefheid overviel hem. Zijn tranen drupten neer op de aarde en verdronken het leven dat hij zojuist had geschapen, waardoor alles onder water kwam te staan. Adam en Eva hadden geprobeerd zich op een berg te redden van de opkomende vloed - maar tevergeefs. Toen, na een lange tijd, de zon de overstromingen had opgedroogd, rezen er twee rotsen dicht bij elkaar op de bergkam van de Ith waar het allereerste mensenpaar de dood had gevonden. Ze worden Adam en Eva genoemd door mensen die niets weten van die vroegere tijden, maar er alleen maar naar kunnen gissen.

properties.name: Trebgast Swimming Lake
properties.description:
The swimming lake in Trebgast offers 60,000 square meters of swimming fun for everyone.

Anyone who enjoys being active will love it here. Swimming, paddle boating, table tennis, and volleyball—it’s all possible. A definite highlight is the island in the middle of the lake—which you can swim to. But this is also the perfect spot for those seeking peace and relaxation. The many seating areas and lounge benches invite you to unwind.

There are changing rooms, restrooms, showers, and baby-changing stations.

For the little ones, there’s a spacious playground where they can run around to their heart’s content. A highlight is the children’s slide located right in the middle of the lake.

A loop trail winding through idyllic natural surroundings is perfect for walking or jogging.

The many access points around the lake are really great, making swimming convenient.

Right next to the lake, there’s a lakeside snack bar with a great relaxation area on the sun deck. It’s a wonderful place to spend some time.

Dogs are not allowed in the swimming area year-round.

Admission is free for children under 6; please check the current prices on site.

The beach volleyball court and the fitness trail are definitely highlights. The many grassy areas for sunbathing and benches are perfect for relaxing.  

A great children’s playground invites kids to run around and play.  

There are showers, changing rooms, and restrooms. The barbecue area is a cozy spot to sit and relax. The snack bar at Kieswäsch provides guests with cold drinks and delicious snacks.  

Not a water lover? How about a walk or bike ride around the lake? The loop trail is well-maintained and offers frequent views of the lake.

properties.name: Church Music at St. Stephan's in Bamberg
properties.description:
Protestant services have been held in the beautiful church on Stephansberg only since 1808. Its founding by Empress Kunigunde over 1,000 years ago, the numerous renovations during the Baroque period, and finally its secularization and transfer to the Protestant Church in 1807 are important milestones in the building’s long history.

The tradition of church music at St. Stephan dates back to the mid-19th century. A choir has existed since 1859, and in 1946, City Cantor Günther Schubert founded the St. Stephan Choir, which still exists today. Under the direction of KMD Werner Krahnert, KMD Ingrid Kasper, and the current deanery cantor Michael Goos, it has since developed into an oratorio choir of national significance. Every year, the Kantorei’s program features several oratorio performances. Members of the Bamberg Symphony Orchestra regularly accompany the choir’s performances as the orchestra. As a parish choir, the Kantorei also enriches the worship services at St. Stephan musically on numerous occasions.  

Two children’s choirs—the Stephansspatzen and the Kinderchor—inspire even the youngest children to take up choral singing and enrich the musical life of the congregation.

The St. Stephan Trombone Choir, under the direction of Walter Forchert, is the visible and audible symbol of the Protestant church’s distinctive character. The “CrossOver” choir, under the direction of Marco Schneider, ventures beyond traditional musical boundaries.

Since 2008, the Mühleisen organ at St. Stephan has been one of the church’s most photographed highlights. Behind the Baroque facade lies a powerful, modern concert instrument on which Deanery Cantor Michael Goos regularly performs in countless musical styles and enriches the church services. 

In addition, the Stephanshof offers wonderful rehearsal facilities for the parish groups of St. Stephan and beyond—with “Musica Canterey Bamberg e.V.” and the “musica-viva-chor bamberg,” both early and contemporary music are represented and shape the vibrant musical life surrounding St. Stephan.

properties.name: Historischer Brauereiausschank Schlenkerla
properties.description:
Mitten in der Altstadt Bambergs, zu Füßen des hohen Doms, liegt der historische Brauereiausschank Schlenkerla. Urkundlich erstmals 1405 erwähnt und heute in der 6. Generation von der Familie Trum geführt, ist er die Quelle von Bambergs Spezialität „Aecht Schlenkerla Rauchbier". Nach alter Tradition wird das Rauchbier hier im Ausschank noch direkt vom Eichenholzfass gezapft. Wer hier nicht eingekehrt ist und nicht den würzigen, unverwechselbaren Geschmack des "Aecht Schlenkerla Rauchbier" gekostet hat, der darf nicht behaupten, in Bamberg gewesen zu sein.

"Schlenkerla" ist längst ein Bamberger Zauberwort geworden, doch wissen viele nicht, wie diese urige Vokabel zustande gekommen ist. Pate stand der Volksmund. Er nannte einen früheren Brauer des Hauses wegen seines schlenkernden Gangs, der die Folge eines Unfalles war, einfach "das Schlenkerla" und verlieh diesen Namen auch dem seit Jahrhunderten bestehenden Brauhaus. Obwohl mittlerweile die sechste Schlenkerla-Brauer-Generation am Faß steht, ist es dabei bis heute geblieben, im 21. Jahrhundert sogar im Internet: www.Schlenkerla.de

**Bierspezialität**: Aecht Schlenkerla Rauchbier

**Bierart/Biergattung**  
untergäriges Vollbier/Märzen (ca. 13,5% Stammwürze, ca. 5,1% Alkohol)

**Brauverfahren**  
Bayerisches Reinheitsgebot

**Aussehen**  
blankes, dunkelbraunes Bier mit einem leicht rötlichen Einschlag, feinporiger, kompakter Schaum

**Geruch & Geschmack  
**kräftig rauch- und malzaromatisch, herb-würzig, mildrezent, vollmundig mit einem markanten Ausklang

**Gesamteindruck**  
Sein nach "frischem Geräucherten" schmeckendes Aroma erhält diese Bierspezialität durch das in der eigenen Mälzerei hergestellte Aecht Schlenkerla Rauchmalz. Ein Original, das man mit herkömmlichen Bieren schwer vergleichen kann und daher etwas gewöhnungsbedürftig ist.

**Bierpflege**  
Trinktemperatur 7-8 °C, mit ordentlicher Borte einschänken

**Weitere Spezialitäten**: Schlenkerla Rauchweizen, Aecht Schlenkerla Rauchbier-Urbock (saisonal), Schlenkerla Lagerbier (nur in Flaschen), Aecht Schlenkerla Fastenbier (saisonal)

properties.name: Die Marsmännla
properties.description:
Immer das Gleiche mit dieser Band: spaßig tanzende, lauthals singende, glücklich lachende Menschen vor der Bühne. Irgendwie scheint es allen außerordentlich gut zu gehen. Was ist da los?!

Die Combo rund um den Antistadl-Festival-Gründer David Saam ist bestückt mit illustren Musikern von Bands wie dem Kellerkommando, Boxgalopp und der Kapelle Rohrfrei. Als grüne Männchen besteigen sie ihre Bastard-Volxmusik-Rakete (Treibstoff: Fränkisches Bier!) und zünden ein schillernd buntes und wundervoll wildes Musikfeuerwerk: Hier werden vertraute Melodien und Texte aus mehreren Jahrhunderten Pop- und Volksmusikgeschichte durch den Schredder gejagt und dann in aufopferungsvoller Handarbeit neu zusammengeklebt. Das Ergebnis ist herrlich verrückte Gute-Laune-Mitsing-Mitspring-Musik, die man einfach lieben muss. Suchtpotenzial extrem hoch und Ratespaß gibt’s noch obendrein!

properties.name: Krippe in St. Otto
properties.description:
